clue.text: Back demanding youngsters taken into custody

parts.note: a demanding person is stern, strict and exacting
wards are children placed under the protection of a guardian or court

explanation.surface: Strict youngsters have been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is an adverb here: towards the stern, the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternwards means towards the rear of a vessel, i.e. moving aft.

clue.text: Caledonian way to retain business

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so the word for way keeps the business abbreviation inside it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A Highland road keeps a firm going.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a native of that country.

clue.text: No longer a farm vehicle — it's used for removals

parts.note: ex- describes something that no longer is, as in ex-wife
a tractor is the standard farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An old tractor gets a new job shifting things.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor is a tool or machine that pulls things out, so it performs removals.

clue.text: Present in London on certain important dates

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the run of letters London on certain

explanation.surface: Someone attends in the capital on certain big occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of London, all of on and the start of certain; 'important dates' only fills out the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: For the nonce means for the present occasion, so the word stands for the time being now.

clue.text: Very old, but getting nice tan maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of nice tan could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: An elderly person acquiring a pleasant suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient is a synonym for extremely aged, belonging to the distant past.

clue.text: Meant not to be seen in action

indicators.note: to be seen in places the word not inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

explanation.surface: Someone intended to remain invisible during the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Denoted and meant are synonyms in the sense of signified or indicated.

clue.text: Look after many an animal sanctuary

indicators.note: after places the word for look behind the Roman numeral for many

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Someone tends a refuge for numerous creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild beast's den, the place where it hides and is safe.

clue.text: A capital forward!

parts.note: capital comes from the Latin caput, head; the capital of a column is its head

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a fine forward player.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means in front or onward, the same sense as going forward.

clue.text: Taking no rest, sent off for turpitude

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of no rest, sent have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone sent away without a break for wicked behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is depravity, and rottenness is moral corruption of the same kind.

clue.text: A lot appear forbearing about a perjurer

indicators.note: about means the word for forbearing goes around the other word

parts.note: mild means gentle, tolerant, forbearing
a perjurer lies under oath, so is a liar

explanation.surface: Many seem tolerant towards someone who lied in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliard is an old British term for a thousand million, a huge number.

clue.text: Frequently expressed as decimal

explanation.surface: A note on how numbers are often written down.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as OF TEN: decimal numbers are based on ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequently means many times; and something decimal is reckoned in tens, based on ten.

clue.text: Self-restrained when happy about batting

indicators.note: about tells us the word for happy goes around the word for batting

parts.note: content means satisfied or happy
a batsman who is batting is in, in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer keeps calm when pleased to be at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means exercising self-control, especially over one's appetites.

clue.text: Order came — sent new window frame

indicators.note: order as a verb means arrange, so the letters of came and sent are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: An instruction arrived to dispatch a replacement window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' strengthens the anagram signal; it is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side, or the frame holding it.

clue.text: Deposit for house

explanation.surface: A down payment on a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to deposit, as in lodging a complaint or funds; a lodge is a small dwelling such as a gatekeeper's cottage.

clue.text: Female centaurs?

parts.note: a centaur is half human, half horse, so a female one would be literally part woman, part horse; really it means women who ride

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about mythological creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Women riders are described with a compound that a female centaur would fit literally.

clue.text: Not the main body of soldiers, so not in mail

definitions.text: Not the main body of soldiers

parts.note: out is the opposite of in, away from home
post is a British word for mail

explanation.surface: Troops detached from the main force are not getting their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small detachment of troops stationed at a distance from the main army.

clue.text: Actor finding love through a "rubbish" write-up

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
per means through or by means of, as in per post

indicators.note: in a down clue write-up means the word for rubbish is written upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A performer gets an awful review in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is one who acts, and an operator is likewise one who works or carries out an action.

clue.text: Compel a fiery beast to go around the ring

indicators.note: to go around puts the word for the fiery beast around the letter for ring

parts.note: a dragon is the fire-breathing beast of legend
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone forces a monster to circle the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon is to coerce or force someone into doing something.

clue.text: Suggestions for introductory music

explanation.surface: Proposals for the opening of a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtures are proposals or approaches made to someone; an overture is an orchestral piece played before an opera.

clue.text: There's too much foam — drawback, that

parts.note: surf is the foam of breaking waves

indicators.note: back tells us the word for draw is read backwards

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game

explanation.surface: Complaining of excess froth as a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' is split: draw gives TIE and back turns it round to EIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, an amount more than is needed.

clue.text: A row caused by suspicion about royalty

indicators.note: about means the word for suspicion wraps around the royal letters

parts.note: a suspicion of something is a trace or hint of it
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A quarrel sparked by doubts about the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A row' is a row of houses, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a line of joined houses built in a continuous block.

clue.text: Ads composed by head with depression

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of ads are rearranged

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring promontories

explanation.surface: Advertisements created by a boss with low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness and depression are both states of unhappiness or low mood.

clue.text: Seat five hundred as arranged

parts.note: a settle is a wooden bench with a high back
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Seating for five hundred as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is an old-fashioned high-backed bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Settled means decided or arranged, as in a matter now settled.

clue.text: Stick with a woman

parts.note: a wand is a thin stick, as a magician's

explanation.surface: Stay loyal to a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanda is a female first name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Alan's awfully nosey!

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of Alan's are in a bad state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that Alan is terribly inquisitive.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's counts here as a letter of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, which is the jokey sense of nosey here.

clue.text: Withdraws touching brochures

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on, as in business letters
tracts are short pamphlets, like brochures

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out a moving set of leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or pull back, the same as withdrawing.

clue.text: A crook to some degree

parts.note: a crook is a bend, and a bend between two lines is measured in degrees; the surface suggests a partly dishonest person

explanation.surface: Someone who is a bit of a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is the bend formed where two lines meet, measured in degrees.

clue.text: Bank genuinely without a single pound

indicators.note: without means the letters for a single pound are dropped from the word for genuinely

parts.note: really means truly or genuinely
a single one is A
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A bank that is truly short of even one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a verb: to bank on, depend.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to depend or count on it.

clue.text: In particular wanting medicos to go down

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, doctors
to fall is to go down

explanation.surface: Especially needing doctors to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Most of all means above everything else, especially.

clue.text: Raven's throat

explanation.surface: The black bird's gullet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raven' is a verb: to eat ravenously.
explanation.definitionFit: To raven is to devour greedily, which is what gorging means; the gorge is also an old word for the gullet.

clue.text: Invalid Greek character accompanied by pupils

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
L is a learner, so two of them are pupils

explanation.surface: A sick Greek with schoolchildren in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' is the adjective (void), not the noun for a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: Null means without legal force, as in null and void.

clue.text: Call for the French cunning? Not necessarily

parts.note: to need something is to call for it
les is French for the (plural)
sly means crafty or cunning

explanation.surface: Is it necessary to ask for clever French people?
explanation.definitionFit: Needlessly means without any need, i.e. unnecessarily.
